items.title: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart: Resting Your Whole Weight on God
items.verse: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths. (Proverbs 3:5-6, KJV)
items.body:
"Trust in the Lord with all your heart" is one of the most quoted verses in the Bible, yet one of the hardest to obey on an ordinary Tuesday when the bill is unpaid, the medical report is bad or the decision cannot wait. Proverbs 3:5-6 does not ask for a feeling. It asks for a transfer of weight: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding."

The Hebrew word for trust here is batach. It pictures a person hurrying to a safe place and lying down there, resting their whole weight, unafraid. David uses it in Psalm 56:3: "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee." So batach is not the absence of fear; it is what you do with your fear. You carry it to the Lord, and you lie down on Him.

Notice the contrast. We are to trust the Lord with all the heart, the whole inner person: mind, will and emotions. We are not to lean on our own understanding. To lean is to put your weight on a staff. Our understanding is God's gift, but it was never built to carry a life. Isaiah compares trusting in human power to leaning on a bruised reed that pierces the hand (Isaiah 36:6). Many of us are limping because we leaned on something never meant to hold us.

In our villages an old rope bed, the charpai, tells the truth about trust. A guest who doubts it sits on the edge, ready to jump. A guest who trusts it lies down and sleeps. Same bed; only one is resting. Faith, as I often tell new believers, is settled trust in a God who cannot lie: resting your entire weight on Jesus, His death for your forgiveness, His resurrection for your life, His lordship over your future. Abraham faced the facts of his old body honestly and was still "fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform" (Romans 4:21). Two convictions held him: God is able, and God is faithful.

How do you trust in the Lord with all your heart today? Name what you have been leaning on: a salary, a relative with influence, your own cleverness. Acknowledge Him "in all thy ways", bringing the decision to Him before you make it, not after. Take the promise as it stands: "he shall direct thy paths." Then write beside your mountain the two convictions that held Abraham: God is able. God is faithful.

This is why someone is praying every hour at the 24-hour prayer tower. Each hour a believer rests on God's faithfulness for people tempted to lean on something else: the family counting coins for medicine, the young believer pressed to deny Christ, the nation trusting its own strength. Proverbs 29:25 says, "The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe." Our persecuted brothers and sisters know that verse by experience. When you take your hour, you join them in the safest place in the world.

Pray with us today for yourself, that you would stop leaning on the one thing you have trusted instead of God and rest your full weight on Him; for persecuted believers pressured to deny Christ, that the fear of man would lose its grip and the Lord would be their safe place; and for the leaders and households of Pakistan and your own nation, that they would seek God's direction rather than their own understanding. Someone needs your prayers. Take your hour at prayertower.church.
items.prayer: Lord, today I choose to trust You with all my heart. Forgive me for leaning on my own understanding and on things that were never able to hold me. I bring You the decision I am facing and the fear I am carrying, and I lie down on Your faithfulness. You are able, and You are faithful. Direct my paths and make them straight. Be the safe place of every believer who is pressed today to deny You, and turn the hearts of the leaders of my nation to seek Your wisdom. In Jesus' name, Amen.

items.title: Intercessory Prayer: Will You Stand in the Gap?
items.verse: And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. (Ezekiel 22:30, KJV)
items.body:
Intercessory prayer is the ministry of standing before God on behalf of someone else. In Ezekiel 22 the city had become like a wall with a hole torn in it; sin had broken the defences and judgment was pouring through. God was not looking for a bigger army or a wiser council. He said, "I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land." Then come four of the saddest words in the Bible: "but I found none." Heaven searched for an intercessor, and the post was empty.

The Hebrew word for intercession is paga. It is an ordinary word meaning to meet, to reach or to fall upon; it describes a traveller arriving at a place, as when Jacob "lighted upon" Bethel (Genesis 28:11). Used of prayer, it means to meet someone with a plea on another person's behalf. Isaiah uses it twice: the Servant "made intercession for the transgressors" (Isaiah 53:12), and God "wondered that there was no intercessor" (Isaiah 59:16). An intercessor, then, is simply a person who goes to meet God carrying a name that is not his own.

Moses shows us what this looks like. When Israel made the golden calf and God spoke of destroying the nation, Moses did not step back from the breach; he stepped into it. "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book" (Exodus 32:32). Psalm 106:23 remembers that day: judgment was turned away because "Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach." Anyone who has lived in a village knows what a broken boundary wall means: until it is mended, someone must stand in the gap through the night, or the animals wander and the thieves walk in. Intercessory prayer is standing in that gap for people who cannot stand for themselves.

How do we practise it today? Name the person, because God sought "a man", one person for one need, not a vague wish for the world. Carry the need as your own, as Moses did when he put his name on the line. Pray the Word over the person, turning promises into petitions. Keep standing; Daniel prayed twenty-one days before the answer broke through (Daniel 10:12-13). And begin with those who have no one to pray for them: the sick neighbour, the backslidden friend, the leaders of your country (1 Timothy 2:1-2), and the villages where no one has yet heard the gospel.

This is why the 24-hour prayer tower exists. A wall is only as strong as its weakest hour, and the tower makes sure that at every hour of the day and night someone is standing in the gap. Many of our brothers and sisters live where a public prayer meeting is impossible; we stand for them, remembering "them that are in bonds, as bound with them" (Hebrews 13:3). When you take your hour, you are the answer to God's search in Ezekiel 22. He is still looking, and this time He need not say "I found none."

Pray with us today for one person by name who cannot or will not pray for themselves, that God would meet them through your standing in the gap; for persecuted believers in hostile places, that the Lord would hedge them about with protection and give them courage where they cannot pray openly; and for the leaders and unreached villages of Pakistan and of your own nation, as 1 Timothy 2 commands. Someone needs your prayers. Take your hour at prayertower.church.
items.prayer: Lord, You are still seeking someone to stand in the gap, and today I answer: here am I. Teach me intercessory prayer. Give me the heart of Moses, who would not step back from the breach, and the patience of Daniel, who kept praying until the answer came. I bring before You the one whose name is on my heart right now; meet them where I cannot reach. Make up the hedge around every persecuted believer who cannot pray openly today. Turn the hearts of leaders and open the villages that have not yet heard. Let it never be said of this hour that You found none. In Jesus' name, Amen.

items.title: Prayer for Revival: Lord, Wilt Thou Not Revive Us Again?
items.verse: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee? (Psalm 85:6, KJV)
items.body:
A prayer for revival is one of the oldest prayers in the Bible, and it was first prayed by people who had already been rescued once. Psalm 85 belongs to a congregation that had come home from captivity. The altar was rebuilt, the songs had started again, yet their hearts were cold and their joy was gone. So they asked the question that still rises from every tired church: "Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?" Revival is not first for the lost. It is for God's own people who are alive on the outside and dry on the inside.

The Hebrew word translated "revive" is chayah, the ordinary word for "to live". In this form it means "to make alive again", to put breath back into something that is fainting. It is the word used when Jacob's spirit "revived" at the news that Joseph was alive (Genesis 45:27). The psalmist is not asking for a new building or a better programme. He is asking God to breathe life back into His people. And the small word "again" tells us he had seen God do it before. Revival is simply God returning to do what He has always done.

When the exiles first came home they laid the foundation of the temple with shouting. Then opposition came, discouragement set in, and the work stood still for about sixteen years (Ezra 4:24). Nothing was wrong with the stones; something had died in the hearts of the builders. God did not send a new budget. He sent a word: "Be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the LORD, and work: for I am with you" (Haggai 2:4). Every great decline begins in the heart before it shows in the field, and every great restoration begins in the heart as well.

How do we pray for revival today? Start where the psalm starts, with yourself: "Turn us, O God" (Psalm 85:4). Confess the coldness honestly, because God revives the humble, not the impressive. Ask for joy, not only for results, for the psalm's goal is "that thy people may rejoice in thee". Pray the Word back to God; Habakkuk did exactly that when he cried, "O LORD, revive thy work in the midst of the years" (Habakkuk 3:2). And do not wait for a better season. Habakkuk asked for revival in the middle of hard years, not after them.

This is the heartbeat of the 24-hour prayer tower. Habakkuk said, "I will stand upon my watch" (Habakkuk 2:1), and the tower is that watch stretched around the clock and around the world. History shows that revival often visits the suffering church first: when the early believers were threatened, they prayed, the place was shaken, and they spoke the Word with boldness (Acts 4:31). In the villages of Pakistan we see it still, as people who have never held a Bible hear the gospel and call on the name of the Lord. Each hour someone keeps in the tower is a small "Wilt thou not revive us again?" lifted for the nations.

Pray with us today for a fresh breath of God on your own heart, your family and your local church; for persecuted believers in hostile places, that pressure would become the furnace of revival rather than the grave of their faith, as it was in Acts 4; and for the nations, Pakistan among them, that God would revive His work in the midst of the years. Someone needs your prayers. Take your hour at prayertower.church.
items.prayer: Father, I come as one of Your own people asking the old question: wilt Thou not revive us again? Turn me first. Where my heart has grown cold, breathe Your life into it. Where my hands have grown slack in Your work, say to me as You said to the builders, "I am with you." Give my church joy in Thee, not only activity for Thee. Revive Your work in the midst of these years, in my home, in my nation and in every hidden church that suffers for Your name. Fill the watchmen in the prayer tower this hour with Your Spirit and Your Word. In Jesus' name, Amen.

items.title: Prayer for the Persecuted Church: Remember Them That Are in Bonds
items.verse: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body. (Hebrews 13:3, KJV)
items.body:
Prayer for the persecuted church is not an optional extra for a few mission-minded believers; it is a command written into the New Testament. The writer to the Hebrews tells us to remember those in bonds "as bound with them", and those who suffer adversity "as being yourselves also in the body". Somewhere today a brother is sitting in a cell for the name of Jesus. Somewhere a sister has lost her home, her work or her family because she would not deny her Lord. Scripture does not ask us to pity them from a distance. It asks us to stand in the chains beside them.

The Greek word translated "bound with them" is sundedemenoi, from sundeo, to be tied together, to be chained to another as a fellow prisoner. This is the only place in the New Testament where the word appears. The picture is two prisoners fastened to one chain: when one moves, the other feels it. That is how God wants His church to feel about its suffering members. "Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it" (1 Corinthians 12:26). Persecution is an injustice that offends the God of love, justice and mercy, yet Jesus called the persecuted blessed and promised them a great reward in heaven (Matthew 5:10-12).

In Acts 12 the apostle Peter was locked between two soldiers, chained, with guards at the door. The church had no lawyer, no influence and no key. But Luke records: "prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him" (Acts 12:5). While they prayed through the night, an angel walked into the prison, the chains fell off and the iron gate opened of its own accord. The believers were so astonished when Peter knocked at the door that they thought it was his angel. Our prayers reach places our feet can never go.

So how do we pray for the persecuted church today? Pray that they will speak the gospel with boldness, as Paul asked for himself from his own prison (Ephesians 6:19-20). Pray that God's grace will be sufficient in their weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9). Pray for the wives, husbands and children left behind. And pray for the persecutors, because Jesus commanded us to bless and not to curse (Romans 12:14). The jailer at Philippi who beat Paul and Silas was washing their wounds and believing in Christ before the night was over. Many persecuted believers do not ask us to pray that trouble will end; they ask us to pray that they will be faithful in it.

This is why the 24-hour prayer tower matters. The church in Acts 12 prayed through the night, and the tower is that praying house stretched across every time zone. When a believer in a hostile place cannot gather, cannot sing and cannot pray aloud, someone in the tower is lifting them to the Father at that very hour. That is sundedemenoi in practice: bound together with them across the miles. In Pakistan we know what it is to be a small flock among many, and we also know the comfort of learning that strangers around the world were praying for us.

Pray with us today for believers imprisoned or on trial for their faith, that they receive strength, boldness and release; for the families of the persecuted and for every request submitted to the tower in the last 24 hours; and for the nations where following Jesus is costly, Pakistan among them, that persecutors meet Christ as the jailer at Philippi did. Someone needs your prayers. Take your hour at prayertower.church.
items.prayer: Father, today I remember my brothers and sisters in bonds as if I were chained beside them. Give the imprisoned Your peace, give the grieving Your comfort, and give every believer who stands before judges the boldness of Peter and Paul. Open iron gates that no human hand can open. Turn the hearts of persecutors as You turned the jailer at Philippi. Forgive me for the days I forgot them, and make my prayers a chain of love that reaches every hidden church on earth. Strengthen every intercessor keeping watch in the prayer tower this hour. In Jesus' name, Amen.

items.title: The Power of Persistent Prayer: Why God Honours Those Who Keep Knocking
items.verse: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint. (Luke 18:1, KJV)
items.body:
Jesus told the story of a widow with no money, no lawyer and no influence. Her only weapon was persistence. Day after day she stood before an unjust judge and said the same words: "Avenge me of mine adversary." The judge cared nothing for God or man, yet her refusal to go away wore him down. Then Jesus made the point that still shakes complacent hearts today: if an unjust judge answers persistence, how much more will a loving Father answer His own children who cry to Him day and night?

The Greek word Jesus used for "faint" is ekkakeo, to lose heart, to grow weary and give up. Persistent prayer is not nagging God; it is refusing to let discouragement close the door that faith has opened. Daniel prayed for twenty-one days before the answer broke through, and the angel told him that his words were heard on the very first day (Daniel 10:12). Delay is not denial. Heaven was moving while Daniel was still on his knees.

This is why a 24-hour prayer tower exists. Around the world, every hour of the day and night, someone is awake and praying. When you grow tired in Lahore, a believer in London takes up the cry. When London sleeps, Los Angeles is interceding. Together the body of Christ becomes a single widow who never stops knocking: for persecuted Christians, for broken families, for the sick, for nations in turmoil. "The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much" (James 5:16). Fervent prayer is persistent prayer.

Whatever you have been praying for, a prodigal child, a healing, a job, a breakthrough for your church, do not faint today. Jesus ended the parable with a searching question: "When the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?" Faith is not proved by one loud prayer but by the quiet prayer still being prayed on the thirtieth day.

Pray with us today for persecuted believers who cannot pray openly, for every request submitted to the tower in the last 24 hours, and for revival in Pakistan and every nation on the prayer wall. Someone needs your prayers. Take your hour at prayertower.church.
items.prayer: Father, forgive me for the prayers I have abandoned too soon. Give me the heart of the persistent widow and the patience of Daniel. Today I lift again every request I had set down, and I ask You to strengthen every intercessor keeping watch in the prayer tower this hour. Let faith be found on the earth, and let it be found in me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
